subject: Dynamic indexing found in a vector of indices

messages.author: f0383747efe2ff95
messages.subject: Dynamic indexing found in a vector of indices
parts:
Hello guys,
When I execute the following nimble model:
GEF.MultiSite.Nimble.test <-  nimbleCode({
  X.mod[1:156] ~ dmnorm(mean = muf[1:156], cov = pf[1:156, 1:156])
  for (i in 1:3) {
    q[i, 1:3, 1:3] ~ dwish(R = aq[i, 1:3, 1:3], df = bq[i])
  }
  if (q.type == 4) {
    for (i in 1:39) {
      start <- obs_per_site[i]*(i-1)+1
      end <- obs_per_site[i]*i
      X[i, 1:3]  ~ dmnorm(X.mod[start:end], prec = q[Ind_block[i], 1:3, 1:3])
      y.censored[i, 1:3] ~ dmnorm(X[i, 1:3], prec = r[i, 1:3, 1:3])
    }
  }
})
I hit the error message as follows:
Defining model Error in getSymbolicParentNodesRecurse(code, constNames, indexNames, nimbleFunctionNames, : Dynamic indexing found in a vector of indices, start:end. Only scalar indices, such as 'idx' in 'x[idx]', can be dynamic. One can instead use dynamic indexing in a vector of indices inside a nimbleFunction. Do you have any idea about how to fix the issue?
Thank you!
Dongchen

messages.author: 9b1f1220a2b07d1e
messages.subject: Re: Dynamic indexing found in a vector of indices
parts:
Hi Dongchen,

I think you'll want to calculate start and end vectors of length 39 in regular R code outside of the NIMBLE model, then provide them to the nimbleModel function in the "constants" list when you build it. You'll then be able to reference X.mod[start[i]:end[i]] for each i in your loop.

NIMBLE uses declarative code to define a network of related nodes at build time. Anything that defines an index--such as start and end in your model, or something like the length of a for-loop--needs to be provided at build time as a "constant" and it can't be modified once the model is built. Also because it's declarative, unlike R, NIMBLE won't loop through and redefine "start" and "end" parameters iteratively--you can only define a given variable once in a NIMBLE model.

Hope this helps--
Ben
